A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same fixed-point generalized random forest work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–F are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original VCM and heterogeneous-treatment-effect simulations, including timings and MSE, plus California housing estimates in Section 7 and Appendix F.

after.justification: V4 reports original simulation and California housing results, including expanded comparisons and new sensitivity experiments in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The fixed-point pseudo-outcomes, CART splitting, honest forest construction, and final weighted estimating equations remain unchanged. Both exact parent estimation and its one-step approximation already appear in v3. V4 explicitly distinguishes these existing variants as GRF-FPT1 and GRF-FPT2; its additional formula does not introduce a new procedure.

E1.justification: VCM, multilevel treatment-effect estimation, and California housing remain the empirical tasks. V4 extends input-distribution coverage through correlated Gaussian-copula auxiliary covariates in Section 6 and Gaussian covariate-correlation scenarios in Appendix D.2, whereas v3's main simulations use independent uniform auxiliary covariates.

E2.justification: V4 adds the exact-parent variant GRF-FPT1 to the simulation and housing comparisons alongside GRF-FPT2 and GRF-grad. The earlier accelerated GRF-FPT corresponds to FPT2, and GRF-grad remains the external baseline. This adds an internal comparator without introducing a broader baseline suite.

E3.justification: Table 1 replaces the earlier tree-count sweeps with large-sample 100-tree and small-sample 100/500-tree grids, adding n = 1,000, 4,000, and 100,000 conditions. Appendix D.2 adds 10-tree protocols extending to 500,000 samples. Appendix C.4 also changes the random-function generator's subset-size rule and center distribution. These are substantive revisions to reported experimental settings.

E4.justification: V4 adds an exact-versus-approximate parent-estimation comparison, the criterion-scale experiment in Figure 2, and sensitivity analyses for auxiliary-covariate correlation, subsampling ratio, and sample-size scaling in Tables 4–6. The original Figure 1 regressor-correlation experiment remains; the new auxiliary-covariate analysis tests a distinct robustness question.

E5.justification: The revised MSE experiments report 50 model replications instead of v3's 40, as stated in Section 6 and the plot labels. Boxplot uncertainty displays and Figure 1's 250 replications with 10th/90th percentile bands already exist in v3. No new confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Simulation timing and MSE results are extensively replaced and expanded under revised conditions, with additional FPT1 and sensitivity results. V4 Table 6 newly reports a 3.08-fold speedup at 500,000 samples. Housing timings remain 19.1 seconds for GRF-grad and 12.6 seconds for the accelerated variant; Table 7 adds FPT1 at 15.4 seconds and 1.24-fold speedup. The revised simulations do not establish same-setting improvements over v3.

T1.justification: Proposition 4.1 changes from equivalence with the unweighted criterion to equivalence with a Jacobian-weighted oracle criterion, adding Neyman orthogonality and an explicit radius/sample-size condition. Appendices A.4–A.5 and B develop this revised argument, add forest-specification Lemma 4.2, prove previously asserted scale invariance, and introduce approximation-consistency Lemma B.5. The consistency and asymptotic-normality theorems are retained and renumbered.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the central claims of faster Jacobian-free forest construction with comparable accuracy and preserved asymptotic guarantees. The quantitative efficiency framing changes: v3's conclusion explicitly claims O(K²) savings, while v4 removes that statement and asserts O(K³) savings in Sections 3.3 and 5.

C2.justification: V4 adds substantive explanations of why iterative fixed-point convergence is unnecessary, discusses varying accuracy rankings and occasional small-sample slowdowns, and attributes weaker HTE speedups to differences from continuous-regressor models. Section 7 adds urban/rural housing interpretations. These extend the earlier brief descriptions of computational gains and similar accuracy.

D1.justification: Appendix C.4 documents selecting FPT1, FPT2, or grad through the method argument. Section 6 and Appendix F newly specify a subsampling ratio of 0.5; this disclosure alone does not establish a changed housing protocol. The code/data links, core pseudocode, and detailed honesty instructions are retained.

R1.justification: V4 adds Cui et al. (2023) on causal survival forests and Yang et al. (2021) on flexible regularized estimating equations. The introduction expands its description of GRF applications, but positioning relative to GRF and the existing fixed-point literature remains substantially the same.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and appendices A–F are retained. V4 makes targeted explanatory rewrites, introduces FPT1/FPT2 terminology, reorganizes proof and simulation subsections, removes a duplicated implementation paragraph, corrects language, and adds acknowledgments. Much of the background, method exposition, and honesty discussion is preserved.

P2.justification: The simulation displays are substantially redesigned and consolidated into grids separating methods, sample sizes, and tree counts. V4 adds the criterion plot and sensitivity tables, expands the housing comparison, recolors the maps, and rearranges appendix figures. MSE axes use a 100-fold display scaling, and Figure 6 corrects the reversed dimensional labels in v3 Figure 10's caption.

improvement.justification: The separate exact/accelerated comparisons and sensitivity tests make the empirical evidence more informative, while the weighted-oracle formulation states the theoretical scope more precisely. However, the new approximation proof has a material gap: Equation (59) treats the regressor–outcome cross-moment as vanishing, although it need not vanish under the stated VCM. The empirical and presentation gains support a limited net improvement, but the expanded proofs do not establish a complete repair of the theoretical justification.
